@dwelle thanks for the thorough review.

>  the GH icon is hardly noticable. Maybe ok.

I tried to make it relatively as visible as it is in light mode, but I'll check to see whether I should it bump it up a bit.

> I'd probably keep the export preview in light-mode, otherwise it may look like we'll export the PNG in dark mode colors:

I think I'd prefer the PNG to be exported in dark mode (if possible). WDYT? (I honestly use screenshoting on macos instead of the export dialog)

> Scene background color picker swatches appear as if transparent:

What do you mean by "transparent"? They are very low contrast but that's true for light mode too.

> I think I'd prefer the PNG to be exported in dark mode (if possible). WDYT? (I honestly use screenshoting on macos instead of the export dialog)

That will be a hard sell. UI scheme shouldn't affect what gets exported. Moreover, if we later change how each color is rendered in dark mode, it would again change export output. Not good.

If nothing else, at least add a checkbox "export in dark mode". But certainly not as a default.

> What do you mean by "transparent"? They are very low contrast but that's true for light mode too.

I mean it gives a feeling as if you took the whole popup and made it `opacity: 0.4` or something. Either way, it's hard to read. I agree that we should leave the swatch colors themselves be, but I'd at least tweak the swatch borders and shortcut hints (make it the same light gray as UI text).

> export dialog name input and buttons are vertically narrower

this is a fix to a bug in prod (you can see the background of the selected icons bleeds out a bit in prod)

I have not changed the swatches, since they kinda match the light version (it could also be improved), and I haven't looked into text selection (I think it can be done separately).

I fixed everything else, and a few other things.

I'll merge this in tomorrow to avoid merge conflicts with other PRs, unless anyone can find a launch blocker :)

Is this planned? If not, I'd be up to implementing it depending on the complexity of the task (seeking input from maintainers on that)

You can of course change the background using the color box, but I'd like to be able to change it based on whether the user has dark mode enabled.
comments: I think that'd be cool. Changing all the colors of the UI and the scene to be dark.

One challenge with this would be handling custom colors but we could apply a transformation like my non-evidence-backed [smart invert color](https://observablehq.com/@j-f1/smart-invert-color) which swaps the S and V channels of the color.

Yes, we should invert the custom colors as well I guess.. that would be interesting :)

This will just be a visual change, right? If you download the file or share it (collaboration) it will all be normal on the other side.

Hah, I wanted to post it here, @Hammster beat me to it!

It's only a visual effect though, the export will still use black lines and white background, and it has issues with lightness and contrast on some colors (though the default ones in the Excalidraw palette seem to work OK). A better color inversion filter would be one proposed by @j-f1 in  https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/1148#issuecomment-606953421.

Edit: I use this technique to add dark mode to Excalidraw SVGs embedded on my blog:
https://francoisbest.com/posts/2020/dark-mode-for-excalidraw

I want this probably more than anything else :) I've been thinking about it:

1) Colors of icons (black to white) should not be just flipped, they're annoyingly bright
2) The rest of the UI needs work, things like "toolbar background" doesn't work flipped (you'll notice this for any dark mode UI, it's not actually inverting, it's darkening)
3) The biggest question though is the color of elements the user can input. I think we should show the color codes as displayed, but stored them in a unified format so that the mode can be flipped (I guess this can be done losslessly by storing as RGB and doing the hue conversion on the fly)
